Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
6:13 PM

UPI has become India's default way to pay because it is free, fast and works almost everywhere. You scan a QR code or type a phone number, approve with a PIN, and the money moves between bank accounts in seconds. No cash to carry, no change to hunt for, no card machine needed.

For small shops, it levelled the field. A tea stall or a vegetable seller can accept digital payments with just a printed QR code. For customers, it removed the need to keep cash handy. Because many banks and apps all work on the same system, people are not locked into one company. Government push and everyday habit did the rest: once your neighbours, your auto driver and your landlord all use it, carrying cash starts to feel odd.

Three main reasons:

Cost: Most person-to-person and small-shop payments carry no fee, so neither side pays extra.
Speed and ease: Payments take seconds, work around the clock, and need only a phone and a bank account.
Reach: From street vendors to big retailers, almost everyone accepts it, so it works nearly everywhere you go.

Figures and rules may have changed, so treat this as a general picture rather than current data.
